name: Bengaluru Tenant Security Deposit Withholding
raw_input: I was renting a 2BHK flat in HSR Layout, Bengaluru for 2 years at Rs 28,000/month. I gave 1 lakh rupees as security deposit. I gave proper 1-month notice on 1st October and vacated the flat on 31st October 2024. I cleared all electricity and water bills and handed over keys. Landlord Mr. Ramesh promised to refund the deposit via UPI in 3 days. Now it has been 25 days, he stopped picking my calls, and yesterday he messaged saying he is deducting Rs 45,000 for 'complete house repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning'. There was no damage, just normal nail holes for photo frames and standard wear and tear. I have move-in photos, move-out handover video, all rent payment bank statements, and WhatsApp chat where he acknowledged receiving the flat in good condition. How can I get my Rs 45,000 back?

case_dossier.case_title: Security Deposit Refund Dispute – Unjust Rs 45,000 Deduction
case_dossier.summary: The tenant vacated a 2BHK flat after two years, handed over keys and cleared dues, but the landlord is refusing to refund the full security deposit and is arbitrarily deducting Rs 45,000 for alleged repainting and cleaning. The tenant possesses photos, videos, payment records, and WhatsApp acknowledgment of good condition.

timeline.event: Tenancy began; tenant paid Rs 1,00,000 security deposit and started paying Rs 28,000 monthly rent.
Tenant gave one‑month notice to vacate the flat.
Tenant vacated the flat, cleared electricity & water bills, handed over keys, and recorded move‑out video.
Landlord promised to refund the full security deposit via UPI within three days.
25 days passed with no refund; landlord stopped answering calls.
Landlord messaged tenant stating he will deduct Rs 45,000 for repainting, marble polishing, and deep cleaning.

evidence_held: Move‑out handover video showing condition of the property
Bank statements showing monthly rent payments and security deposit payment
WhatsApp chat screenshot where landlord acknowledges receipt of flat in good condition
Copy of the rent/lease agreement (if available) – mentioned as likely possessed
evidence_needed: Original signed rent/lease agreement specifying terms of security deposit and permissible deductions
Receipt or acknowledgment of the Rs 1,00,000 security deposit payment
Written notice (email/WhatsApp) from landlord stating the Rs 45,000 deduction and detailed justification
Any repair/cleaning invoices or quotations that the landlord claims justify the deduction
Inventory or condition checklist (if any) prepared at move‑in and move‑out
Proof of settlement of all utility bills (bills or clearance certificates)
case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: The tenant has strong documentary proof of payment, condition at handover, and landlord's acknowledgment, but lacks the formal lease terms and detailed deduction justification, preventing a perfect score.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing: You have a solid legal right to get back the full security deposit you paid. Under the Model Tenancy Act (where it applies) and the Transfer of Property Act, a landlord can only keep part of the deposit for genuine damage that goes beyond normal wear and tear. The photos, videos and the landlord’s own WhatsApp message confirming the flat was in good condition show that the deductions for repainting, marble polishing and deep cleaning are not justified. Because you handed over the keys and cleared all dues, the law requires the landlord to refund the deposit within 30 days of you vacating. This is a civil matter – it is about recovering money, not about a criminal offence.

governing_laws.relevance: Caps security deposit at 2 months’ rent and obliges the landlord to refund it within 30 days after peaceful possession is handed over, allowing deductions only for genuine, itemised losses.
Defines ‘reasonable wear and tear’; ordinary fading of paint or minor marks cannot be charged against the deposit.
Requires the tenant to hand over possession at the end of the lease, which you have done.

governing_laws.act_name: General Legal Principle (Civil vs. Criminal Boundary)
governing_laws.relevance: Clarifies that a dispute over a security‑deposit refund is civil, not a criminal cheating case.

action_options.title: Send Formal Legal Demand Notice
action_options.cost_estimate: Free to minimal (speed‑post or email, plus nominal postage)
action_options.details: Draft a polite but firm notice citing Model Tenancy Act [unverified reference removed] & Transfer of Property Act Sec. 108(B)(m). State that the deposit of Rs 1,00,000 must be returned in full within 15 days, with interest for delay, and attach copies of your move‑out video, photos and the WhatsApp acknowledgment. Send it by registered post/e‑mail and keep a copy for your records.

action_options.title: File a Grievance on the State Rent Authority / Rent Court Portal
action_options.cost_estimate: Zero court fees for claims up to Rs 5 Lakhs (as per State Rent Authority rules)
action_options.details: If the landlord does not comply, log in to your State’s Rent Authority portal (or the National Consumer Helpline 1915 for guidance). Upload the notice, payment proof, move‑out video, and the landlord’s deduction claim. Request an order for refund of the full deposit plus interest.

action_options.title: Petition the Rent Authority / Small Causes Court
action_options.cost_estimate: Nominal filing fee (usually a few hundred rupees) plus any stamp duty, if applicable
action_options.details: Prepare a petition stating the facts, attach all evidence, and cite the relevant sections of the Model Tenancy Act and Transfer of Property Act. You can appear in person without a lawyer. The authority can order the landlord to refund the deposit, pay interest, and may also award a modest compensation for wrongful deduction.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: You can handle the notice and the filing yourself; the rent‑authority and small‑causes courts allow self‑representation. A lawyer becomes useful only if the landlord contests the claim aggressively, files a counter‑claim, or if you need help drafting the petition. In that case, consult a lawyer or seek free assistance from the District Legal Services Authority (15100).
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self‑advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

Acknowledgement copy to be kept as proof of service.)* --- ### **3. Subject** > **Demand for Refund of Security Deposit (Rs. 1,00,000) with Refund of Unjust Deduction of Rs. 45,000 within 15 Days** --- ### **4. Under Instructions of My Client / The Undersigned Submits as Under** 1. **Tenancy Details** - **Commencement:** Around **Oct 2022** – a 2‑BHK flat was let on a written lease (copy annexed). - **Security Deposit Paid:** **Rs. 1,00,000** (receipt annexed). - **Monthly Rent:** **Rs. 28,000** (paid regularly – bank statements annexed). 2. **Notice to Vacate** - On **1 Oct 2024**, the tenant served a one‑month notice as per the lease, expressing intention to vacate on **31 Oct 2024**. 3. **Vacating & Handover** - On **31 Oct 2024**, the tenant vacated the premises, cleared all electricity & water dues, handed over the keys, and recorded a **move‑out video** (Annexure‑C) showing the flat in good condition. - A WhatsApp message dated **31 Oct 2024** from the landlord acknowledges receipt of the flat in “good condition” (Annexure‑D). 4. **Landlord’s Promise & Subsequent Default** - Within **3 days** of vacating (early Nov 2024), the landlord assured the tenant that the **full security deposit** would be refunded via UPI. - By **25 Nov 2024**, **25 days** had elapsed with **no refund** and the landlord stopped answering calls. 5. **Arbitrary Deduction Claim** - On **26 Nov 2024**, the landlord messaged the tenant stating that **Rs. 45,000** would be deducted for “re‑painting, marble polishing and deep cleaning” without furnishing any invoice, quotation, or itemised bill. 6. **Evidence in Possession** (strong documentary proof) - Move‑in photographs (Annexure‑A) - Move‑out video (Annexure‑C) - Bank statements showing deposit & rent payments (Annexure‑B) - WhatsApp acknowledgment of good condition (Annexure‑D) - Copy of the lease agreement (Annexure‑E) – **original signed lease** to be produced on demand. --- ### **5. Legal Grounds** | **Statute / Principle** | **Relevant Provision** | **Application** | |--------------------------|------------------------|-----------------| | **Model Tenancy Act, 2021** (where applicable) | [unverified reference removed] – Refund of security deposit within **30 days** of peaceful possession; deductions only for **genuine loss** beyond normal wear & tear. | Landlord has no right to retain Rs. 45,000 without itemised proof of actual damage. | | **Transfer of Property Act, 1882** | Sec. 108(b)(m) – “Reasonable wear and tear” cannot be charged to the tenant. | Ordinary repainting/cleaning after two‑year tenancy is normal wear & tear. | | **Transfer of Property Act, 1882** | Sec. 108(b)(q) – Tenant must hand over possession; tenant has complied. | Entitles tenant to full refund of deposit. | | **Indian Contract Act, 1872** | [unverified reference removed] – Interest at **12% per annum** for delayed payment of a sum due. | Landlord’s failure to refund within 15 days attracts statutory interest. | | **Consumer Protection Act, 2019** (if landlord is a “service provider”) | Right to **redressal of deficiency** in service. | Tenant may approach Consumer Forum as alternative remedy. | --- ### **6. Demand** > **You are hereby directed to:** > 1. **Refund the entire security deposit of Rs. 1,00,000** (i.e., **Rs. 55,000** after deducting the unjust Rs. 45,000) **plus** interest at **12% per annum** calculated from **27 Nov 2024** till actual payment. > 2. **Pay the amount of Rs. 45,000** which has been **unjustly withheld**, together with the above interest. > 3. **Make the payment** by **NEFT/UPI** to the following account: > - **Account Name:** ______________________________ > - **Bank:** ______________________________ > - **IFSC:** ______________________________ > - **Account No.:** ______________________________ > **The above payment must be effected within **15 (fifteen) days** from the receipt of this notice, i.e., on or before **____________________**.** --- ### **7. Consequence of Non‑Compliance** If the demanded amount is **not received** within the stipulated 15‑day period, **the undersigned** will be constrained to initiate **legal proceedings** without further notice, which may include: 1. **Filing a complaint before the State Rent Authority / Rent Court** under the Model Tenancy Act and Transfer of Property Act for recovery of the deposit, interest, and **damages** for wrongful deduction. 2. **Approaching the Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum** (if applicable) for compensation. 3. **Claiming litigation costs, attorney’s fees, and statutory interest** as per the provisions of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908 and the Indian Contract Act. *All costs incurred thereafter shall be borne by the landlord, together with the principal amount and interest.* --- ### **8. sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Mr. Ramesh, as per Section 108 of the Transfer of Property Act and the Model Tenancy framework, ordinary wear and tear like wall paint aging cannot be deducted from my deposit. I have the handover video and our chat proof. Please refund my balance 45,000 within 7 days.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Dekho bhai, aapka jo Section 108 ka zikr hai, woh property transfer ke liye hota hai, rent‑lease ke liye nahi. Hamare lease agreement mein clearly likha hai ki 'any repainting or deep cleaning required beyond normal wear and tear will be deducted from the security deposit'. Aapke video aur chat se humara kaam nahi rukta – humne aapko ek detailed invoice bheja tha, aur aapke agreement ke clause 7(b) ke mutabik humare paas deduction ka haq hai. Company policy ke hisaab se, deposit ka final settlement 30 din ke andar hota hai, aur aapka 7 din ka demand unrealistic hai. Agar aapko koi problem hai, to aap legal notice bhej sakte hain, hum bhi apni taraf se proper notice de denge.

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: You correctly cited a specific statutory provision and presented concrete evidence (photos, videos, chat) to back your claim, which forces the landlord to acknowledge the seriousness of your demand.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: Mention the exact clause in the lease agreement that prohibits such deductions and reference the Consumer Protection Act ([unverified reference removed]) for unfair trade practices. Also ask for an itemised bill for the alleged repainting costs.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: Please send me the itemised invoice and the exact lease clause that allows a Rs 45,000 deduction, or I will file a complaint under the Consumer Protection Act.
